_comment: Synthetic schema example for /api/identity.schema.v1.json. This file is NOT a snapshot of any production identity — it is a fixed demonstration of the schema's shape. It demonstrates the post-2026-08-14 kind discipline: entries whose kind is 'stream' carry NO sha256 on purpose (their bytes change without a commit, so a signed digest could not survive), while 'static' and 'record' entries do. The live /api/identity.json takes this shape from its first re-issue on or after 2026-08-14; manifests signed before that date pin every listed artifact, including streams, and those stream pins are known-stale by construction (deploy/identity-pin-baseline.json). All sha256, fingerprint, hash, and timestamp values shown here are synthetic placeholders that document field formats only; they do not refer to any real artifact, key, or moment in time. Production runtime identity is published at /api/identity.json by scripts/operator-local/gen-identity.sh on the operator's local Mac (signed with the operator identity ed25519 key; the validator's staker.key / BLS signer.key are not used). Phase α A-chain anchoring is reached via the pointer field anchor_receipt_url (added 2026-06-21). The former dag_root_hash and cycles_history_url fields were RETIRED 2026-07-06 (design-stocktake #1 DAG-root collapse) — the single on-chain root is anchor-source.json.dag_root_computed (3-branch), surfaced via anchor-receipt.json, not a field on identity.json. See docs/IDENTITY_SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md.

pin_policy.rule: An artifact_manifest entry carries sha256 only when the publication registry declares its kind as 'static' (bytes change only when a commit changes them) or 'record' (immutable bytes at a URL that never resolves differently). Entries with kind 'stream' are published with url + kind and NO sha256: their bytes change without a commit, so a digest fixed at signing time would be false within minutes. The absence of sha256 is a deliberate declaration, not an omission, and a verifier MUST NOT treat it as a broken manifest. The same rule is applied independently to schema_url / schema_sha256.
pin_policy.merkle_leaves: artifact_root is the Merkle root over exactly the sha256 values present in artifact_manifest, in alphabetical key order.
